top.title: 3 takeaways as Victor Wembanyama's double-double leads Spurs to seventh straight win
top.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) defends Sacramento Kings forward Domantas Sabonis (11) during the first half of an NBA basketball game on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. (AP Photo/Jose Luis Villegas) (Jose Luis Villegas/Associated Press) SACRAMENTO, Calif. - Victor Wembanyama cooled off a bit, but it didn't stop him from leading his team to yet another win. Wembanyama finished with 30 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks, Stephon Castle had 19 points and a team-high seven assists, and the Spurs crushed the Sacramento Kings 124-109 Friday night for their seventh straight win in the opening game of NBA Cup group play for both teams. The Spurs' winning streak is the longest in the league this season. Wembanyama's modest - by his standards - stat line came after his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block masterpiece in a 112-111 victory over Dallas on Wednesday night at the Frost Bank Center. "I expect Victor to play the right way," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said when asked if there was a minimum amount of points he expects his star player to produce each game. "He obviously has a tremendous amount of gravity in terms of putting the defense in a tough spot when he's putting pressure on the rim and running the floor and rolling after screens. And I think that's going to produce points, but there are teams that have made very concerned efforts at times of taking that away. And what that should do then is open up opportunities for his teammates." That happened against the Kings in the form of Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell scoring 19 points each on a night the Spurs hit 15 of 30 shots from 3-point range. "We've got a team well-built," Wembanyama said. Said Harper, "We're at our best when everyone's touching the ball, everyone's getting to the paint, kicking out, just making the right play. And it's just a byproduct of our chemistry and how much we generally enjoy playing with each other." Playing on the first night of a back-to-back that ends in Portland and the first outing of a four-game road trip, the Spurs (7-2) took a 19-point lead into halftime Friday after Wembanyama scored 20 points and eight rebounds. Playing 26 minutes overall, he finished 10 of 18 from the field and 4 of 6 from beyond the arc. With his fourth 30-point game of the season and seventh double-double, Wembanyama joined Shaquille O'Neal (1993-94) and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (1975-76) as the only players to post 250 points, 100 rebounds and 35 blocks in the first nine games of a season since blocks became official (1973-74). Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 22 points on an inefficient 9-of-20 from the field to lead the Kings, who fell to 1-8 with their second loss in a row. Domantas Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and five assists for Sacramento. The start of the game was delayed for about 20 minutes due to a mechanical issue with the basket the Spurs shot at during warm-ups. top.title: ‘Some legends don't say goodbye’: Ex-India cricketer's heartfelt message for Mohammed Shami after Test retirement
top.description: Former India cricketer and ex-Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary paid an emotional tribute to Mohammed Shami after the veteran fast bowler announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 12-year career in the longest format. Tiwary, who had the opportunity to lead Bengal with Shami in his bowling attack, took to X to reflect on the pacer's impact and recall his association with the speedster. He described Shami as a warrior, while also highlighting the lasting memories he had created through his performances in the red-ball format. "The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history," Tiwary wrote. — tiwarymanoj (@tiwarymanoj) Recalling his time as Bengal captain, he added: "This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart" Shami's announcement brings an end to an impressive Test career spanning 64 matches, during which he picked up 229 wickets. The 36-year-old made the announcement through an Instagram post, confirming that while he would no longer represent India in the white jersey, he intended to continue playing white-ball cricket. "I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote. "Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added. A 12-year journey in India's Test colours Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. His ability to extract movement through seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a crucial member of India's pace attack across different conditions. Of his 229 wickets, 131 came in 35 Tests played in South Africa, the West Indies and India, where he maintained an average of under 25. South Africa witnessed some of Shami's finest performances in Test cricket. During India's 2018 tour, he produced a match-winning spell of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test, helping the visitors secure a consolation victory. On India's subsequent visit to the country, he continued his impressive record by claiming eight wickets in the series-opening Test at Centurion. Shami's final appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's. Injuries later disrupted his career, and he remained out of the Indian team after the 2025 Champions Trophy, before deciding to bring his red-ball journey to a close.

top.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives two match points to end Taylor Fritz's ATP Finals hopes
top.description: Carlos Alcaraz survived two match points against Taylor Fritz to book a spot in the last four of the Paris Masters and end his opponent’s hopes of reaching the ATP Finals. In a lengthy contest that lasted two hours and 43 minutes, the second seed lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3. Had Fritz taken one of his opportunities in the second set, he would have locked down the eighth and last place in the end-of-year championship. Instead, that spot now goes to Alcaraz’s fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar. After being outlasted by Fritz in the opener, Alcaraz had to save match points with and against serve in the second, before levelling the scores with three games in a row. He belatedly took control as he closed out the decider in clinical fashion. Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges await the Spaniard in the semi-finals. “I tried not to let myself down in the difficult moments in the second set,” Alcaraz said. Carlos Alcaraz is into the semi-finals of the Paris Masters (Getty) “I tried to stay strong mentally and save those break points and match points. I used the people and the energy and gave them what they really wanted to watch. “I am really happy to play for one and a half hours more to entertain them. The feeling I have today is unmatched.”

top.description: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that have affected the team this season. According to SPORT , sporting director Deco is examining several possibilities, although the club’s limited financial flexibility in January means finding an affordable reinforcement will be a significant challenge. Barcelona decided against recruiting a central defender during the summer, directing their resources towards strengthening midfield and attack instead. However, an accumulation of defensive injuries exposed the squad’s lack of depth, increasing the urgency to reinforce the position before the second half of the season. Given Barcelona’s financial condition, Deco is exploring loans, affordable transfers and opportunities involving players whose contractual situations could make them accessible. Fikayo Tomori and Vitor Reis among Barcelona’s defensive options On that note, AC Milan’s Fikayo Tomori is one of the leading names under consideration. The English defender’s contract expires in 2027, and Milan are reportedly open to negotiating his departure in January. Interest from several Premier League clubs could nevertheless create competition for his signature. Barcelona are keeping tabs on Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images) Manchester City’s Vitor Reis is another possibility . The Brazilian has struggled for regular opportunities, accumulating just 199 minutes across four appearances this season. A temporary move could offer him valuable playing time, although there is no indication that City are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the season. Piero Hincapie also attracts Barcelona’s attention because of his versatility. The Ecuadorian can operate at both centre-back and left-back, making him particularly suitable for Flick’s defensive requirements. In fact, Deco has already sounded out his representatives about a potential loan with an option to buy. top.title: New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final
top.description: Stacey Waaka has represented New Zealand in rugby sevens, rugby union and rugby league [Getty Images] New Zealand (8) 32 Tries: Wiki, Waaka 3, Hufanga, Atai, McGregor Goals: Kiria-Ratu 2 Samoa (0) 0 New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final. It will be the Kiwi Ferns' seventh successive appearance in the showpiece match, but having won the first three between 2000-2008, three trips to the final since then have all ended in heartache. Three consecutive losses to Australia included a blowout 54-4 scoreline four years ago at Old Trafford and unless debutants Fiji spring one of the greatest upsets in the tournament's history in the other semi-final, the Jillaroos are likely to again provide the substantial obstacle to New Zealand becoming four-time champions. However, on Saturday, New Zealand made light of the blustery and difficult conditions inside Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, to make their case as potential winners. Mackenzie Wiki's try - less than two minutes into proceedings, off the back of a Samoa error - set the tone for the Kiwi Ferns. As the storm clouds began to gather overhead, New Zealand's dual-code international Stacey Waaka capitalised on some indecision from Samoa winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala to collect and ground Raecene McGregor's kick. It was efficient and highly professional from New Zealand, who conceded just 24 points across their three group games and once again exhibited their defensive parsimony during a hard-fought first period. A combination of that and Samoa's inability to make the most of field position, with a smattering of handling errors thrown in as well, laid the platform for New Zealand's triumph. There were notable bright spots for the Samoa fans to enjoy. Fanua Rimoni was a powerful and dominant presence at lock forward, while teenage winger Anastasia Leatupue produced a nerveless showing on her international bow. Samoa's biggest disappointment was that they could not get the ball into the hands of the 18-year-old in good attacking positions - with Pauline Piliae-Rasabale twice pulled up for forward passes on the right edge in an error-strewn display. But just like in the first 35 minutes, they had no answer to New Zealand's more potent attacking threat. Waaka was again the beneficiary of a pinpoint McGregor kick as she crossed for her second try and Mele Hufanga held off the attentions of three Samoa defenders tfor her score. It was a feat that was matched by Kaiyah Atai just over two minutes later as New Zealand went through the gears. With Samoa's resistance gradually waning, Waaka capped a fine individual display with her hat-trick and McGregor scored the try her performance richly deserved to round off a fine New Zealand display. top.title: Paraguay Senate impeaches President Peña, VP Alliana takes over
top.description: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts. Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links. Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent. Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment. “Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP. Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters. Alliana promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno Bank’s takeover amid insolvency concerns. “Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated,” said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. Opposition lawmakers had also filed a motion to impeach Alliana over the crisis, but the request failed to gain congressional approval. – Money trickles back – The bank’s demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno. Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, a Central Bank official told AFP. The first phase of aid deposits, up to around $1,600, will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, said Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund. The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he added. Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that have stripped him of political immunity. The opposition accused the US-backed politician of a conflict of interest, which he denied. The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.” He will be questioned over alleged crimes of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds on Saturday, prosecutor Gonzalez Vester said. Pena urged reconciliation in an X post shortly before his removal. “Today, we must come together as Paraguayans to rebuild our institutions and restore trust,” he said. top.title: 24 ‘pointless races’ in 10 years: Formula 1 has an end-of-season problem
top.description: Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP’s final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year’s Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi . Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective. Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton ’s all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit. Verstappen lost out in last year's title showdown with Lando Norris (Getty) But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers’ title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport’s ultimate prize on the line. There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory. This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness. Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the “battle for second” or the “best of the rest” tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that. Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten. top.title: Islam Makhachev Drops Major Hint About Retirement, Could Follow Khabib Nurmagomedov’s Lead
top.description: Islam Makhachev’s future in the UFC has been a major talking point over the past few days. The reigning welterweight champion drew plenty of criticism from fans and pundits after reportedly pulling out of negotiations for a fight at UFC 336 . Makhachev was initially expected to defend his 170-pound title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card. However, those plans fell apart after the Dagestani stepped away from the proposed matchup. The champion later explained that the welterweight division had several deserving contenders and believed Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate inside the Octagon. However, the fight negotiations aren’t the only reason Makhachev’s future has come under scrutiny. The two-division champion recently turned 35 on October 27 and has openly discussed the possibility of retirement. He has suggested that he doesn’t have many fights left and wants to spend the remainder of his career facing the toughest available competition. Now, he has offered another hint that his retirement might be closer than expected. Islam Makhachev Says He Will Listen to His Mother When It Comes to UFC Retirement During a recent interview with Red Corner MMA in Tashkent, Makhachev suggested that his career could come to an end much like that of Khabib Nurmagomedov. Interestingly, their mothers could have a say in both decisions. For those unfamiliar, ‘The Eagle’ retired at 32 after promising his mother that he wouldn’t fight again without his father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Following Abdulmanap’s passing ahead of UFC 254, ‘The Eagle’ decided to honor that promise . The Dagestani went on to secure his 29th professional victory against Justin Gaethje in Abu Dhabi before announcing his retirement inside the Octagon. Makhachev now appears to be considering a similar path. He said, “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” The former lightweight champion also admitted that he doesn’t have a specific number of fights in mind before calling it a day. However, he made it clear that he feels his career is nearing its end. top.title: Windows takes a break at UK motorway services
top.description: A roadside display at Cherwell Valley services has stopped dispensing information and started asking for help. The eagle-eyed Register reader who spotted the stricken screen told us: "UK motorway signs often tell us that tiredness can kill, urging us to take a break. This poor thing at Cherwell Valley services took the advice to heart." The display at the Moto services appears to have run into trouble during a restart. Windows offers another attempt or access to repair tools, although the latter options are hidden – perhaps somewhere on the top floor of the neighboring Travelodge. Getting things moving again will probably require access to the computer behind the screen. The Automatic Repair screen is all too familiar to Windows users. Not to be confused with the classic blue screen of death, it might indicate a misbehaving driver during a reboot, an update that did something unexpected, or some sort of hardware failure. Hopefully it isn't the latter – with memory and storage prices the way they are at the moment, a motorway services sandwich or gallon of fuel will seem a positive bargain by comparison. Our reader is right: taking a break is sensible advice. Getting Windows to end one can be another matter. ®

top.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
top.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. Dončić scored a season-high 53 points, including 20 in the third quarter, as the Lakers overcame a 16-point deficit to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 124-118 on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. top.title: Devils stay top with overtime victory against Stars
top.description: Cardiff Devils wore a one-off bespoke uniform, with the game against Dundee Stars designated 'country night'. [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November. Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display. Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error. The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second. Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff. "It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson. "We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner." Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).

top.title: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important”
top.description: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important” Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with the club bringing in a number of stars to bolster the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. One such player who arrived with high expectations at the Santiago Bernabeu was Marc Cucurella. The World Cup winner was expected to be the player who would improve Madrid’s squad the most in a position that has been problematic since Marcelo’s exit. Cucurella explains what makes playing for Real Madrid different Representing Los Blancos has come with expectations that have far exceeded what Marc Cucurella initially anticipated. The Spaniard has now reflected on the unique responsibility that comes with wearing the Madrid shirt. “Being a Real Madrid player means that every match against another team is hugely important to them, perhaps the biggest match of the year,” the Spanish international explained. Cucurella has talked about the challenges of playing for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Having spent years at Barcelona coming through La Masia ‘s ranks, Cucurella understands both perspectives. “When I used to play against Madrid, that week was special: everyone wanted to come and see you, and they wrote to you,” he recalled. “Ultimately, having the responsibility of winning every match is a wonderful thing and easy to handle.” Facing Real Madrid is always a big occasion for their opponents, but playing for Los Blancos is a whole different challenge. A responsibility Cucurella is learning to embrace Cucurella had a difficult start to life at Real Madrid but has come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella is embracing his new life in the Spanish capital. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) His performances have coincided with Los Blancos ‘ upturn in form, and the Spaniard has firmly established himself as Jose Mourinho’s first-choice left-back. Cucurella is also facing significant competition from Alvaro Carreras, who has done nothing wrong in the chances Mourinho has given him. Between them, the manager has two high-quality options who can start on any given day, and that is a luxury to have. Cucurella will hope to put in a good performance against Valencia later tonight as Madrid look to extend their winning run to eight games. It remains to be seen how the Spaniard fares over the course of the season and how the battle between him and Carreras pans out. Source: RMTV

nigeria.title: Paraguay Senate impeaches President Peña, VP Alliana takes over
nigeria.description: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts. Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links. Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent. Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment. “Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP. Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters. Alliana promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno Bank’s takeover amid insolvency concerns. “Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated,” said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. Opposition lawmakers had also filed a motion to impeach Alliana over the crisis, but the request failed to gain congressional approval. – Money trickles back – The bank’s demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno. Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, a Central Bank official told AFP. The first phase of aid deposits, up to around $1,600, will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, said Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund. The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he added. Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that have stripped him of political immunity. The opposition accused the US-backed politician of a conflict of interest, which he denied. The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.” He will be questioned over alleged crimes of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds on Saturday, prosecutor Gonzalez Vester said. Pena urged reconciliation in an X post shortly before his removal. “Today, we must come together as Paraguayans to rebuild our institutions and restore trust,” he said. nigeria.title: How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Passengers inside a commercial bus, popularly called Danfo in Lagos were stunned when a fellow passenger suddenly went into sudden labor and successfully gave birth to a baby boy on board. According to Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the woman was traveling across the state when labor began unexpectedly mid-journey In the process, fellow commuters and onlookers quickly assisted her through the delivery inside the vehicle while others went into prayer session for safe delivery. Medical responders and local commuters assisted in securing the mother and child immediately following the emergency delivery. Fortunately, after few minutes, the baby boy was delivered safely. In viral footage capturing the moments following the birth, witnesses suggested naming the child Abiona—a traditional Yoruba name commonly associated with a child born on a journey or along the road. Recall that a similar incident happened at Onipanu Bus Stop, along Ikorodu Road sometimes ago. “In a swift r​esponse, LASEMA arrived at the scene to assist a pregnant woman who went into sudden labor while waiting for transport. “The woman delivered a healthy baby boy. His apparent references to Peter Obi’s handling of erosion in Anambra and Atiku Abubakar’s departure from the PDP sought to turn their past decisions into questions about their fitness to govern. These were campaign accusations, rather than independently established assessments of their records. Vice-President Kashim Shettima reinforced the attack, questioning Obi’s credibility and arguing that Atiku’s experience should be judged by accomplishments rather than years in office. His assertion that Obi has lost goodwill remains a partisan assessment; it does not establish a measurable change in voter support. The political intention is clear: put the challengers on the defensive. That matters for an incumbent whose own performance is under examination. If voters spend more time debating whether the opposition is credible, the government gains room to argue that continuity is the safer choice. But scrutiny travels both ways. Once the campaign becomes a comparison of records, Tinubu must also answer for the results of his presidency: purchasing power, security, employment and public services. nigeria.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
nigeria.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. nigeria.description: Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. nigeria.title: Trump: Lesson for Nigeria, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: Donald Trump wanted the November 3 midterm elections to be about him. He said so repeatedly, urging Americans to vote as though his name were on the ballot. He wanted a Republican victory to demonstrate that his presidency still commanded popular support and that his influence over American politics remained firmly intact. Well, Americans took him seriously. Perhaps more seriously than he expected. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major electoral setback to Trump and his Republican Party. Yet, as the results became clear, Trump reached for an explanation that seemed to contradict his own campaign message. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he declared: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The irony is difficult to miss. He had spent weeks asking Americans to treat the election as a verdict on his presidency. When the verdict went against him, he suddenly appeared to be distancing himself from it. He wanted the political benefits of making the election about him without accepting the consequences when voters delivered an unfavourable answer. For readers in Nigeria, it is worth explaining what America calls midterm elections and why they matter. In the United States, a president is elected for a four-year term, but congressional elections take place every two years. This means that halfway into a president’s tenure, Americans return to the polls to elect members of the legislature. These elections are called midterms because they take place in the middle of a presidential term. Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the 100 Senate seats contested every two years. Midterm elections do not determine who becomes president. The sitting president remains in office. Instead, voters decide which party controls Congress and, by extension, how much support or opposition the president will face in the legislature This gives Americans an opportunity to express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with a president’s performance without waiting another four years. They can strengthen the president’s party in Congress or hand control to the opposition, making it considerably more difficult for the president to advance his legislative agenda. That is precisely what has happened to Trump. American presidents often benefit from what is known as the coattail effect. When a president is popular, candidates from the same party can benefit from that popularity. His political strength becomes an advantage for others seeking elective office. But when a president becomes unpopular, the effect can work in reverse. Candidates associated with his administration may find themselves paying the price for public dissatisfaction with his leadership. nigeria.title: From open pavilion to nation of orderlies: Is Zik’s ‘fear-free’ Nigeria still possible?
nigeria.description: .What a 1960 inauguration says about fear in today’s corridors of power By Omeiza Ajayi Nearly 66 years after Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was sworn in as Nigeria’s first African Governor-General, the footage of that day – which has again recently gone viral – raises an uncomfortable question: why did a leader who held the highest office in the land need no retinue of security details standing behind him, while today every minister, and even some local government supervisors, cannot move without a swarm of details? The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. The narrator of the newsreel set the scene plainly. “At the steps of the pavilion stand the Prime Minister and the Lord Chief Justice, symbolising the people and the law, on what is surely one of the most important occasions in the history of the country.” No armed escort looms in the frame. No aide hovers at the shoulder of the man the crowd was chanting for. “Zik! Zik!” rang around the square as he arrived, and the vast stands, in the narrator’s words, were “hushed.” Today the picture is reversed. In Abuja and in the state capitals, orderlies trail ministers into halls and offices. The situation is so bad that some security personnel actually enter into very enclosed spaces or rooms with their AK47 rifles in clear breach of security protocol. At the local government level, some unelected supervisory councillors have been known to move with armed vigilance team members or hunters, sometimes to intimidate the very people they were appointed to serve. The easy explanation is insecurity, and it is not a false flag. Banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have made parts of the country dangerous, and no leader can be faulted for fearing for his life. But the leaders of other nations also face threats. Behind the American president or a British prime minister stand trained protective officers, assigned to a defined danger. They do not crowd every public official, from the cabinet room to the ward office, with men whose chief duty is to announce importance. It is not uncommon in Nigeria to see security details standing and blocking a television camera. That leaves the harder question. Are Nigeria’s leaders afraid of the general state of the country, or have they become afraid of their own people? Zik, standing in the open that November morning, appeared to have settled that question for himself. He began his address with these words: “It is with humility, mingled with joy, that I thank this grand concourse of patriots and friends of Nigeria for congregating here today on the occasion of my inauguration as the first African Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of the Federation of Nigeria.” He titled the speech “Respect for Human Dignity,” and he made no secret of what he feared for Nigeria. nigeria.title: Police rescue 10 stolen children in Abia
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered from them. The CP said one of the suspects had confessed to belonging to the Black Axe Confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other members of the gang. nigeria.title: Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. nigeria.title: Nigeria is losing $1.6bn yearly to avoidable blindness — Aghaji
nigeria.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru Almost on a daily basis, across Nigeria and much of Africa, millions of people wake up to a world they cannot see clearly. A farmer peeks at his cassava farms for instance, but cannot differentiate the difference between weed and crop. A trader holds her register at arm’s length, guessing at figures she once read at a glance. A child in the back row of a classroom copies from a board that is almost a blur. More often, an old woman needs her grandchild to lead her to the market because the road she walked for over 50 years has become unrecognizable. Those are not statistics. They are the human face of a crisis that Africa has lived with for too long. As Professor Ada Aghaji told a packed hall at the University of Nigeria on October 29, 2026, this is a crisis Africa can no longer afford to ignore. Delivering the institution’s 254th Inaugural Lecture, titled “Let There Be Sight: Building Sustainable Eye Health Systems for All in Africa,” Aghaji, Professor of Ophthalmology and Eye Health Systems, made a simple but very powerful argument: eye health in Africa is not just a medical issue. It is an economic issue. A development issue. A justice issue. And the numbers prove it. According to her, Nigeria loses an estimated $1.6 billion every year in productivity because of vision impairment. Across Africa, the loss is about $9 billion. Globally, it stands at a staggering $410 billion. Behind those figures are livelihoods cut short, schooling interrupted, and families pushed deeper into poverty. Yet, as Aghaji stressed, much of this vision loss can be prevented or treated. A pair of spectacles costing less than a bag of rice. A 15-minute cataract operation. A routine screening at a primary health centre. Why, then, do millions of Africans continue to live with avoidable blindness when the solutions already exist? That was the question at the heart of her lecture. Two Children, Two Worlds Perhaps the most haunting moment of the lecture came not from statistics, but from a story. Aghaji spoke of two children born with congenital rubella syndrome; a condition that can cause cataracts, deafness and other disabilities. One was born in Nigeria. He faced delays, barriers to treatment and rehabilitation, and ended up blind. The other was a Somali refugee child in England. He received timely surgery, spectacles and hearing aids, and with them, a chance to learn, to play, to grow Their medical conditions were similar. Their opportunities were profoundly different. The contrast, Aghaji argued, is the story of Africa’s eye health system in miniature. Medical knowledge alone does not guarantee care. What determines whether a child sees or goes blind is often not the disease, but the system around it: whether there is money to pay, a health worker to detect the problem, a referral that works, a hospital that can be reached. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. sports.title: 3 takeaways as Victor Wembanyama's double-double leads Spurs to seventh straight win
sports.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) defends Sacramento Kings forward Domantas Sabonis (11) during the first half of an NBA basketball game on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. (AP Photo/Jose Luis Villegas) (Jose Luis Villegas/Associated Press) SACRAMENTO, Calif. - Victor Wembanyama cooled off a bit, but it didn't stop him from leading his team to yet another win. Wembanyama finished with 30 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks, Stephon Castle had 19 points and a team-high seven assists, and the Spurs crushed the Sacramento Kings 124-109 Friday night for their seventh straight win in the opening game of NBA Cup group play for both teams. The Spurs' winning streak is the longest in the league this season. Wembanyama's modest - by his standards - stat line came after his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block masterpiece in a 112-111 victory over Dallas on Wednesday night at the Frost Bank Center. "I expect Victor to play the right way," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said when asked if there was a minimum amount of points he expects his star player to produce each game. "He obviously has a tremendous amount of gravity in terms of putting the defense in a tough spot when he's putting pressure on the rim and running the floor and rolling after screens. And I think that's going to produce points, but there are teams that have made very concerned efforts at times of taking that away. And what that should do then is open up opportunities for his teammates." That happened against the Kings in the form of Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell scoring 19 points each on a night the Spurs hit 15 of 30 shots from 3-point range. "We've got a team well-built," Wembanyama said. Said Harper, "We're at our best when everyone's touching the ball, everyone's getting to the paint, kicking out, just making the right play. And it's just a byproduct of our chemistry and how much we generally enjoy playing with each other." Playing on the first night of a back-to-back that ends in Portland and the first outing of a four-game road trip, the Spurs (7-2) took a 19-point lead into halftime Friday after Wembanyama scored 20 points and eight rebounds. Playing 26 minutes overall, he finished 10 of 18 from the field and 4 of 6 from beyond the arc. With his fourth 30-point game of the season and seventh double-double, Wembanyama joined Shaquille O'Neal (1993-94) and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (1975-76) as the only players to post 250 points, 100 rebounds and 35 blocks in the first nine games of a season since blocks became official (1973-74). Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 22 points on an inefficient 9-of-20 from the field to lead the Kings, who fell to 1-8 with their second loss in a row. Domantas Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and five assists for Sacramento. The start of the game was delayed for about 20 minutes due to a mechanical issue with the basket the Spurs shot at during warm-ups.
